story.title: Putin's United Russia Party Secures Majority in Parliamentary Elections
story.summary: Vladimir Putin's ruling United Russia party has achieved a record majority in the recent parliamentary elections, winning approximately 58% of the vote. The elections, which have faced criticism for being tightly controlled, resulted in United Russia securing 355 out of 450 seats in the Duma. Additionally, 49 veterans of the Ukraine war were elected to the new parliament, further consolidating the party's influence.

event_overview.title: About Russia Elections
event_overview.subject: Russia Elections
event_overview.summary: Russia’s 2026 parliamentary election chooses the ninth convocation of the State Duma, the elected lower chamber of the Federal Assembly. Voting is being held during Russia’s war against Ukraine and alongside regional and municipal elections; the political environment has been marked by restrictions on opposition activity.

facts.label: Voting period
facts.value: Voting for the 2026 State Duma election is scheduled across three days, September 18–20, 2026; September 20 is the single voting day.

facts.label: Institution being elected
facts.value: The State Duma is the lower chamber of Russia’s Federal Assembly (parliament) and has 450 deputies.

facts.label: Electoral system
facts.value: The election uses a mixed system: 225 deputies are elected in single-member districts and 225 from federal party lists in proportional representation.

facts.label: Term and election authority
facts.value: State Duma deputies serve five-year terms. Under the federal election law, the president calls regular Duma elections, while election commissions administer the process under election legislation.

facts.label: Voter and candidate eligibility
facts.value: Russian citizens aged 18 or older may vote; a candidate for the State Duma must be at least 21 and permanently reside in Russia, subject to other legal qualifications and restrictions.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline covers the opening of voting on September 18, 2026, rather than the full campaign, regional contests, vote count, certification, or longer-term political consequences.

explore_lenses.label: What changed in the Duma’s balance of power?
explore_lenses.title: A larger governing supermajority
explore_lenses.summary: Preliminary results point to United Russia expanding its already dominant position, giving it well above the two-thirds threshold used for some high-level parliamentary actions. That does not mean it can change the constitution by itself.

claims.text: With more than 95% of precinct results counted, the Central Election Commission said United Russia was projected to win 355 of 450 Duma seats, exceeding its prior record of 343 seats in 2016.
The projected total includes United Russia candidates leading in 208 of the 225 single-member districts, alongside its party-list result of about 57.8%.

A two-thirds Duma vote is sufficient for adoption of a federal constitutional law, but such laws also require approval by three-quarters of the Federation Council; amendments to constitutional chapters 3–8 additionally require approval by at least two-thirds of Russia’s regional legislatures.

points: With more than 95% of precinct results counted, the Central Election Commission said United Russia was projected to win 355 of 450 Duma seats, exceeding its prior record of 343 seats in 2016.
The projected total includes United Russia candidates leading in 208 of the 225 single-member districts, alongside its party-list result of about 57.8%.

A two-thirds Duma vote is sufficient for adoption of a federal constitutional law, but such laws also require approval by three-quarters of the Federation Council; amendments to constitutional chapters 3–8 additionally require approval by at least two-thirds of Russia’s regional legislatures.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The 355-seat figure was described as preliminary on September 21, 2026; final certification and any post-election challenges were not established in the reporting consulted.

explore_lenses.label: What does the veterans’ bloc signify?
explore_lenses.title: A visible wartime presence in parliament
explore_lenses.summary: The incoming Duma is set to include dozens of people who served in Russia’s war against Ukraine, reflecting the Kremlin’s effort to place veterans in public office. Their election does not by itself show how they will vote or what policies they will pursue.

claims.text: Officials said 49 people who took part in the war against Ukraine were elected to the new Duma; United Russia General Secretary Vladimir Yakushev had initially said 86 veterans were likely to win before revising the figure to 49.
Before the vote, election officials said nearly 200 candidates had served in Ukraine, while the Kremlin presented veterans as a new national elite for civilian leadership roles.

The election also included voting in Ukrainian regions Russia annexed in 2022, which Moscow says helps incorporate those territories while Ukraine and most of the international community reject the annexations.

The election also included voting in Ukrainian regions Russia annexed in 2022, which Moscow says helps incorporate those territories while Ukraine and most of the international community reject the annexations.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The available reporting identifies the number of veterans elected but does not establish a shared legislative agenda or whether they will act as a cohesive bloc.

explore_lenses.label: What happens before the new Duma starts work?
explore_lenses.title: Certification, then a first sitting
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate result is preliminary; after mandates are formalized, the new chamber must organize itself. Its first meeting is normally due 30 days after the election, although the president may call it earlier.

claims.text: The reported seat allocation was based on near-complete rather than final returns, so the official completion of vote tabulation and allocation of mandates remains a necessary step before the chamber is fully constituted.
Under the Duma’s rules, the new State Duma convenes for its first meeting on the 30th day after the election unless the president calls it earlier.

Before that sitting, a temporary deputies’ working group prepares the agenda and organizational arrangements; at the first sitting, deputies elect the Duma chair and other initial bodies by open vote.

story_report.summary: Near-complete results in Russia’s parliamentary election put Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party at about 57.8% of the vote and projected it to win 355 of the 450 seats in the State Duma. The total would exceed the party’s previous high of 343 seats in 2016, consolidating its parliamentary dominance. Officials also said 49 people who participated in the war against Ukraine were elected to the new chamber.

sections.heading: Duma Majority and Constitutional Legislation
sections.body: United Russia’s projected result combines its party-list vote with candidates leading in 208 of the 225 single-member districts. A two-thirds vote in the Duma is sufficient to adopt a federal constitutional law, although such legislation also requires approval by three-quarters of the Federation Council. Amendments to constitutional chapters 3 through 8 require an additional approval vote from at least two-thirds of Russia’s regional legislatures.

sections.heading: Veterans and Annexed Ukrainian Regions
sections.body: Before voting, election officials said that nearly 200 candidates had served in Ukraine, while the Kremlin portrayed veterans as a new national elite for civilian leadership positions. United Russia General Secretary Vladimir Yakushev initially said 86 veterans were likely to win seats before revising the figure to 49. The vote also took place in Ukrainian regions annexed by Russia in 2022; Moscow says this aids their incorporation, while Ukraine and most of the international community reject the annexations.

sections.heading: Duma Certification and First Sitting
sections.body: The reported allocation was based on near-complete, rather than final, returns, leaving official tabulation and mandate allocation to be completed before the chamber is fully constituted. Under Duma rules, the new legislature meets for the first time on the 30th day after the election unless the president calls it earlier. A temporary working group prepares the session, at which deputies elect the Duma chair and initial bodies through an open vote.

unresolved.text: The sources did not establish when results would be finally certified, whether post-election challenges would arise, or when the inaugural sitting and election of the Duma chair would occur.
Available reporting does not establish whether the 49 elected war veterans will pursue a shared legislative agenda or operate as a cohesive bloc.

related_stories.title: Media Outlets Sue Trump Administration Over White House Coverage Ban
related_stories.summary: CNN, Politico, and MS NOW have announced plans to sue the Trump administration after being banned from White House coverage. The outlets argue that the ban is unconstitutional and a violation of the First Amendment. Following the ban, other major networks have also declined to provide pool coverage of President Trump's activities.

related_stories.title: Kremlin Party Secures 355 Seats in Russian Parliament Amid Controversial Elections
related_stories.summary: In recent parliamentary elections, Russia's pro-Putin party achieved a record 355 seats, maintaining its dominance in the State Duma. The elections were characterized by allegations of being tightly controlled, with an anti-war party failing to meet the threshold for representation. Reports indicate that the voting process was heavily monitored, including instances of armed soldiers overseeing ballot submissions.
